1301.author: HongyeZhou
1301.body:
## Problem

Version numbers of an Artifact came from one number instead of from the versions actually stored: `createArtifactVersion` used `artifact.currentVersion + 1` and an import wrote a package's own numbering with no uniqueness check (`services/api/src/store.ts`). A catalogue where the pointer lagged behind the versions on disk (written by an older build, restored, merged by hand) handed out a number that already existed, and an import could re-create a collision outright. Two versions of one Artifact then both read as "v3", so the version list, `latestReportVersion`, research-snapshot copies, by-number lookups and every reference that pins `(artifactId, version)` became ambiguous.

## Change

- `createArtifactVersion` allocates `max(highest stored number, artifact.currentVersion) + 1`, skipping numbers already stored for that Artifact, so a lagging pointer cannot hand out an existing number. A pointer that is not a whole number is treated as `0` instead of turning the allocation into `NaN`.
- `load()` normalises a catalogue that already holds duplicates: within one Artifact the first number in `(createdAt, id)` order is kept, every later collision moves above that Artifact's highest number, and `currentVersion` is lifted to the highest number that actually exists. Lifting the pointer also removes the false `ARTIFACT_VERSION_CONFLICT` that a lagging pointer produced when the newest version was published as an edit.
- The normalisation skips Artifacts whose numbers are all usable and unique, so a well-formed catalogue is not touched, and it tolerates hand-edited data: only safe positive integers count as numbers, a missing or non-string `createdAt`/`id` no longer throws while ordering, and a `currentVersion` that is not a whole number is reset before the per-Artifact lift. Without that, one malformed row made `load()` reject (the API could not start), three rows without usable numbers made it loop forever, and a deleted pointer survived every reload.
- An import keeps the package's numbers exactly, because `research-snapshot-integrity` compares each `version` and `currentVersion` and because provenance (`evidenceItems[].origin.artifactVersion`, numeric memory-graph properties) resolves by number. The package is validated before any session, Artifact or version is created: a number that is not a positive integer is refused with `ARTIFACT_VERSION_INVALID` (the restore would skip it and leave the provisional number behind, which collides just as badly) and a number used twice for one Artifact with `ARTIFACT_VERSION_DUPLICATE`, so a refused import leaves no partial catalog behind.

I renumbered on load instead of refusing to load: the issue leaves that sub-question to the maintainer, and a refusal would strand every session whose catalogue already has such a version. No version ID changes, so dependencies and references are untouched.

## Tests

`services/api/src/store.test.ts`:

- `Artifact versions are numbered above the stored versions, not from a stale currentVersion pointer` writes `currentVersion: 0` into the persisted catalogue after two versions exist, expects the pointer to be lifted to `2` on load, and expects an edit published against the newest version to succeed as `3` (that path used to fail as a stale base).
- `a catalog holding duplicate Artifact version numbers is renumbered on load` writes two versions under number `1`, expects `[1, 2]` after `load()`, the same numbers and IDs on a second load, and the next allocation to be `3`.
- `an import keeps the package's own version numbers` restores a normally numbered package onto a fresh Artifact and asserts `[1, 2]` with `currentVersion === 2` (the numbers `createArtifactVersion` provisionally allocated must not shift), then `5` while free (`[1, 5]`).
- `a package with a repeated or unusable Artifact version number is rejected before anything is created` (`research-package-http.test.ts`) rebuilds the evidence package twice — two versions under number `1`, then `[0, 1]` — posts each to a fresh project, expects `400` with `ARTIFACT_VERSION_DUPLICATE` and `ARTIFACT_VERSION_INVALID`, and asserts the project still has no Artifacts.
- `a catalog with malformed version numbers and timestamps still loads` writes a non-numeric number, a missing `createdAt` and a duplicate, expects three distinct usable numbers, then deletes `currentVersion`, reloads, and expects the pointer to be lifted and the next allocation to be a real integer.

The first, second and last fail on the base revision; the package case fails when the up-front validation is stashed, and the import-numbering case failed on the renumbering variant reviewed at `cc407a35`.

## Verification

- `pnpm ci:l1` — PASS, planned 4 / passed 4 / failed 0
- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` at the repository root, and `pnpm typecheck` in `services/api` — clean
- `node --import tsx --test src/store.test.ts` in `services/api` — 135 tests, 135 pass, 0 fail
- `node --import tsx --test src/research-package-http.test.ts` in `services/api` — 29 tests, 29 pass, 0 fail (the import path the second change touches; it failed on `cc407a35`)
- Full `services/api` suite in this worktree — 2476 pass / 8 fail. Every failure is environmental: missing `services/paper/.venv` (the three PDF cases), missing `sciencediscovery_evolve` (the protocol and IdeaTree cases), user namespaces (the Runner case), and the two `API runs ... subagent` cases, which fail the same way on the untouched base `bbdbdd5c`. None of them touches Artifact versions.
- No user-visible surface changes, so no screenshots apply.

Fixes #1300

1312.author: yuanzhou75
1312.body:
Refs #1311

**This addresses the most likely cause of #1311, and it is now verified by execution — but it is not a complete fix for that issue.** Two remaining gaps are listed at the end, so #1311 stays open.

## The problem

`/idea-tree <task>` is deliberately not intercepted: it is sent as an ordinary message, so the agent has to decide by itself to call `create_idea_research` (`apps/desktop/src/idea/command.ts` documents this). The skill that tells it to do that is `skills/idea-tree-team`, and skill selection reads the frontmatter `description`:

```yaml
description: Prepare supplied inputs for autonomous Idea Tree research and explain its saved results.
```

That names no command and contains no literal `/idea-tree`. A message starting with `/idea-tree Skip literature retrieval. Explore low-cost iron catalysts…` therefore contains "Idea Tree" only as a hyphenated command name, while the task subject (catalysts, water treatment) matches `structure-pocket-inspection`, a domain skill in the same catalog. Selection mode is `all` by default (`DEFAULT_SKILL_SELECTION_MODE`, asserted in `services/api/src/selected-skill-defaults.test.ts`), so the right skill is present; it simply was not the one chosen.

## Observed failure

`test/journey-idea-tree-real.spec.ts` on head `a5f028cd`, two runs, same prompt and settings:

| Run | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | passed — `1 passed (8.2m)`, model called `create_idea_research` after 72s |
| 2 | failed — 180s card wait expired; the agent was still exploring at round 4 (`list_files` → "Writable workspace is empty" → `$SCIENCEDISCOVERY_SKILLS_DIR/structure-pocket-inspection` → `run_shell` → `Run stopped`) and never called `create_idea_research` |

Ruled out: the sandbox (the same `mkdir` command succeeds standalone) and the selector (run 1 used the identical locator). Tracked as #1311.

## Change

One field, no instruction text:

```yaml
description: "Use when the composer message starts with /idea-tree or /idea-tree-team,
  or the user explicitly asks for autonomous Idea Tree research: prepare supplied
  inputs for the research and explain its saved results."
```

The workflow text below the frontmatter is untouched, and no runtime behaviour changes — only what the selector is told this skill is for.

## Validation — two consecutive passing runs

Head `e4410b801417833e89d24cfba4f189c2e9123881`, same head, two runs of `test/journey-idea-tree-real.spec.ts`, each with its own result directory:

| Run | Exit | Result | Case body | Stack health |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | **0** | `1 passed` | 11.3 min (wall 689s) | `200 / status:ok` 10s after start |
| 2 | **0** | `1 passed` | 8.5 min (wall 524s) | `200 / status:ok` 10s after start |

Frontmatter checked independently before running: `yaml.safe_load` on this head's `SKILL.md` returns a dict with keys `['description','name']`, `description` length 207.

**Environment, stated precisely.** `http://127.0.0.1:4310` — default port, and **not an isolated data directory**: the run used the repository default `.sciencediscovery-data`, because `start-stack --mode local` reads the repository `.env`, which overrides an exported `SCIENCE_DISCOVERY_DATA_DIR`. Backend **`legacy`** (`--no-node-build --no-jiuwenswarm`). Model `http://113.46.219.251:8080/v1` with `DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017`. WSL Ubuntu / linux-amd64. Only `skills/idea-tree-team/SKILL.md` was replaced, and it was restored afterwards.

## The invalid-YAML detour on the previous head

The first version of this change wrote that description **unquoted** (head `667368d7`, blob `bbd0fe23`). It contains `research: prepare` — a colon followed by a space — which in a plain YAML scalar is a mapping indicator, so the frontmatter failed to parse:

```
SKILL.md frontmatter is invalid YAML: Nested mappings are not allowed in
compact mappings at line 2, column 14
```

A skill package that fails to load took the whole API down: every route, `/health` included, answered 400. That is what broke the stack probes, not a probe defect and not isolation behaviour — the same `.env`, port and token answered 200 only once the staged file had been restored, i.e. the two probes were reading different file contents.

Quoting the value makes the colon ordinary text. Verified after the fix: `yaml.safe_load` on this head's frontmatter parses cleanly, so the failure mode is gone at the source. Lesson recorded for anyone editing this field: a `description` containing `": "` must be quoted.

## What #1311 still needs after this

1. **The alternative hypothesis is not excluded.** If selection ignores `description` phrasing and is driven instead by how the prompt orders or presents the selected skill list, this change would not be the cause — two passing runs raise confidence but do not prove the mechanism.
2. **Backend coverage.** All evidence is `legacy`; the daily profile defaults to `jiuwenswarm`. Nothing has been verified there, for this PR or for the journey.

If either needs code, it belongs in #1311's follow-up rather than here.

## Release

Release category: release:fix
User impact: none directly — skill selection for `/idea-tree` gains an explicit signal.
Compatibility and migration: none.

1314.author: agent-ci-infra-bot[bot]
1314.body:
A malformed bundled Skill file used to reject startup, and every route — `/health` included — replayed that `SKILL_VALIDATION` as 400. A broken package is now contained to that skill: both built-in loading paths catch validation per package, log it, skip it, keep the rest; `/health` answers 503 while starting or unavailable, and the by-id route answers 404 for a failed bundled id. This revision also resolves the conflict with `main` `d13cead`.

## What changes

1335.body: ## Summary The 0.4.0-rc1 account-center acceptance run (Issue #1223) failed on three acceptance criteria and left two P3 observations. This fixes everything that a code change can fix: the ledger's balance column was not additive, a renamed nickname was overwritten on the next sign-in, the seven-day reward strip highlighted the wrong day, the signed-out account panel had no way back and still offered a credits model whose token had just been revoked, and credits printed as `895.877`, which reads as a thousands separator in Chinese. The only reported item left open is D5 (installer not code-signed, Defender firewall prompt); it belongs to the release certificate process, not this repository. Refs #1223 ## The ledger's balance column now continues the ledger `settleCredits` recorded the spendable balance at settle time. That figure already has any second call's hold subtracted from it, while the hold itself has no ledger row, so with two calls in flight the older row dropped by the other call's hold and the next row gained it back — exactly the ±2.227 pair the report found in the 11/20 15:52 batch. The row now continues the previous row's `balance_after`, which makes "previous balance + delta = this balance" hold for every row. Rows and the spendable balance agree again once no hold is open; the top-of-page balance is still the account's own figure, not a second computation. The rule is one helper (`services/accounts/src/ledger.ts`: `ledgerAfter` + `appendLedger`), and **every** writer goes through it — the settle, the sign-in REGISTER/CHECKIN/BONUS rows and the admin adjustment. The previous version fixed only the settle while the grants still wrote `credit_accounts.balance`, so a grant during an open hold broke the chain and the error propagated into every later settle; that is the case zhaozhaozz's P2-1 and the bot's F1 describe. Every writer also takes the `credit_accounts` row (`SELECT … FOR UPDATE`) before it inserts. `settleCredits` and `adjustCredits` already did; `signIn` inserted its CHECKIN/BONUS rows before any lock, so under READ COMMITTED a concurrent settle could read an older row, compute a higher id, and leave a pair that is not additive. With the lock taken first, the insert order matches the id order the ledger endpoint returns. ## A saved nickname survives the next sign-in `signIn` wrote `display_name = COALESCE($2, display_name)`, so the HUAWEI profile name the client re-sends on each sign-in replaced whatever the user had saved. The column is now filled only while it is empty (`COALESCE(display_name, $2)`): the first sign-in still seeds the profile name, and a rename survives a sign-out and the next account. Avatar and email keep following the profile. The trade-off is deliberate: once seeded, the column is frozen, so a name changed on the provider side no longer propagates for a user who never renamed here — tracking "user set it" separately would be the way to have both. ## Reward strip, decimals, signed-out panel - `rewardProgress()` derives the strip from the check-in count and whether today is already in the ledger. Four check-ins with today paid now highlights the fourth slot, so the highlight and "3 more days" add up to seven. Before today's sign-in the next claimable day is still the one marked. - The count itself now comes from `GET /v1/me` (`checkins: { total, lastDate }`, counted in SQL), not from the loaded ledger page. The page is capped at 100 rows, so on a busy account today's CHECKIN fell out of it and a paid day rendered as pending (the bot's F4). Older services that do not send `checkins` fall back to the page count, which is what the screenshots below were taken against. - Credits always render with three decimals (`895.877`, `900.000`, `4.123`) alongside the existing thousands grouping. - The signed-out account panel gets a back-to-sessions control, and while no account is signed in the composer withholds the credits model and says why — the provider stays in the catalog, so signing back in needs no setup. ## Validation - `tsc -p apps/desktop/tsconfig.json --noEmit`, `tsc -p services/accounts/tsconfig.json --noEmit`, `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit`: clean. - `services/accounts` tests: **45 pass / 0 fail**. `ledger.test.ts` drives the real SQL through a fake `Queryable`, so reverting `appendLedger` to the spendable balance, or `adjustCredits` to an absolute `balance`, fails it (this is the coverage zhaozhaozz's P2-3 and the bot's F3 asked for); the route tests add a grant-while-a-hold-is-open case that asserts both the chain and the final agreement with the page balance, and the existing rename and two-hold cases. - `apps/desktop` tests: **206 tests, 89 pass, 0 fail, 117 skipped** (skips are the `os:linux`-tagged suites, including the new `account-reward-progress` case, which CI runs). - Walked through by hand in the browser, in `zh` and `en`: account page (credits, strip, ledger), sign-out, and the signed-out composer and model picker. Captures below. ## Screenshots The web build of this branch (`apps/desktop/dist`) served by the local control plane, signed in with a HUAWEI account against the production accounts service. The three-decimal credits, the seven-day strip and the signed-out surfaces are rendered by this branch; the client here is the built `apps/desktop` output, not a separately patched page. Ledger rows older than the fix (11/20 15:52) are shown exactly as they are stored — that historical pair is the bot's F2, not something this PR rewrites. **Account page, `zh`** — credits `895.877 / 900.000 / 4.123`; the strip marks days 1–4 done with the fourth as today, and the hint says `再连续 3 天可获满 7 天奖励 +50 积分`; every row's `余额` continues the row below it (`897.262 → 897.249 → 897.226 → 896.138 → 895.877`). **Signed-out account panel, `zh`** — `返回会话` at the top left, and the HUAWEI sign-in button; the panel no longer traps the user. **Signed-out composer, `zh`** — the model pill reads `积分模型需要登录华为账号后才能使用` and the send button is disabled. **Model picker while signed out, `zh`** — only `DeepSeek-V4-Pro` and `添加自定义模型`; the credits provider's models are withheld while no account is signed in. **`en`** — `Back to sessions`, `Sign in with HUAWEI ID to use the credits model`, and a picker listing only `DeepSeek-V4-Pro` and `Add a custom model`. The images live on the throwaway `pr-1335-assets` branch (`pr-assets/1335/`) so the description renders them inline; nothing is added to this PR's tree, and the branch is deleted once this lands. ## E2E user journeys Not run locally: the affected paths need a live accounts service (Postgres, HUAWEI OAuth callback) plus a packaged client, and a second concurrent model call to reproduce the hold interleaving. The desktop changed in the composer and the account page only; no browser journey was added. ## Release Release category: release:fix User impact: the account page's ledger reconciles row by row, a renamed nickname stays, the seven-day strip stops contradicting its own hint, and signing out leaves a usable panel and a model picker that does not offer a dead token. Compatibility and migration: no schema change. Existing ledger rows keep their stored `balance_after`; new rows continue from the latest one, so an old break stays visible in history but does not propagate. `GET /v1/me` gains `checkins: { total, lastDate }`; the desktop treats it as optional, so an older accounts service keeps working with the page-count fallback.

1336.body:
## What

Let a macOS installation opt into direct (unsandboxed) local code execution — the same two-door contract Windows already runs — and make the boot flow **sandbox-silent**: initialization neither blocks nor mentions the sandbox anywhere; the ONE place sandbox health is surfaced is a status row in 设置 › 通用 (owner decision, 2026-11-23).

A single commit (squashed from the review iterations — the tree is identical to the last-reviewed head `6bd586c3` plus the F26 fix). The change reads in four waves:

**Wave 1 — the opt-in (backend + desktop wiring):** `sandboxForPlatform` reads the installation flag before answering seatbelt for darwin; `start-stack` whitelist takes provider `none`; 设置 › 通用 switch + preload bridge + per-spawn env pair (`SCIENCE_AGENT_SANDBOX_PROVIDER=none`, `SCIENCE_AGENT_EVOLVE_UNISOLATED=1`); integration pin feeding the decision straight into preflight.

**Wave 2 (U5) — the boot stops gating:** a failed probe degrades to a logged session flag + the direct provider pair; the fail-closed error page and its authorization block are retired. *(Superseded by U5c below — see the red-lines section.)*

**Wave 3 (U5c) — the boot goes silent; monitoring lives in Settings alone:** the one-shot probe moves to `app.whenReady` (before the wizard/normal split — first-run wizard sessions now probe too), failure leaves zero UI trace (log + env + the settings status row), the wizard self-check list drops its Seatbelt entry (api/runner/model), the wizard's banner copy and fail-closed gate are gone, and `seatbelt-error.html` is deleted. New: the settings status row (green / amber / muted) + `sd-shell:seatbelt-status-get` IPC + the full-blast-radius hint.

**Wave 4 — review fixes (F12/F14/F15/F16/F17/F18/F19):** the row derives its state from the spawn-time `directActive` snapshot AND the probe verdict — it states the live stack's mode, never the persisted switch's value, and never claims "sandboxed" while the session runs direct; the failed line carries a localized cause (structured `failCode`) with raw reason + diagnostics on the dot's tooltip; non-darwin verdicts normalize to `null` (the row is darwin-only); the copy names every cost of the mode (R execution refused — Python only, persistent sessions/kernels unavailable); the dot keeps its 10px under the stack-row width rule.

## The contract (unchanged doors, one new key)

The Windows contract has two doors: an installation-level opt-in, and a per-run confirmation in pre-flight (`unisolated_run_unconfirmed` refuses an unconfirmed run). This PR ports exactly that to darwin:

- **Per-run confirmation: zero changes.** The whole chain reads the backend value, not the platform — the moment darwin answers `direct`, the existing EvolveCreateDialog banner + confirmation dialog, the `--allow-direct` command write, the read-back check, the triple-AND in proposal and the pre-flight refusal all light up untouched. Integration-tested end to end.
- **Default installs with a healthy sandbox: bit-for-bit unchanged.** `sandboxForPlatform` returns seatbelt exactly as before unless the opt-in file says `"1"`; a probe that passes changes nothing anywhere.
- **Fail-closed state hygiene:** the persisted state parses only an exact `"1"` — truncated or hand-edited files read OFF; failed reads read OFF.

## The red lines, third revision (U5c: settings-only)

Three comments in the merged code say variations of "darwin never does this", and #1165's acceptance list said "a Seatbelt failure never reaches the main UI… no forward button". **The owner's decision (2026-11-23) retires the fail-closed red line itself**, and goes further than U5 did: initialization is sandbox-silent — no gate, no banner, no self-check entry; the probe is a health check whose verdict shows in 设置 › 通用 alone. The defense:

1. `bootstrap.ts` "darwin NEVER sets it": the env pair is injected per-spawn only when the opt-in file says so or the session's probe actually failed — same shape as the win32 hard-set.
2. `evolution/sandbox.ts` "unavailable → refuse": the opt-in changes what "available" means for that installation, matching the documented Windows contract rather than carving out a macOS exception.
3. The acceptance "a Seatbelt failure never reaches the main UI… no forward button" — **retired**. A failed probe no longer blocks or marks the boot at all; the session continues with the direct provider pair, and the settings status row is where the user learns what mode they are in. What still guards **evolution candidate runs** is the second door: the per-run confirmation in pre-flight (`unisolated_run_unconfirmed` refuses an unconfirmed direct candidate), the same door Windows uses — the user is always told what running unsandboxed means and confirms **each candidate run** before it executes. The Agent's own ephemeral Shell/Python under provider `none` does **not** pass through that door — there is no per-run dialog on those routes; their unsandboxed mode is disclosed by the settings status row and governed by the switch (设置 › 通用), exactly what the settings copy states ("程序演进每次运行前仍会单独确认").

Why settings-only rather than a boot banner (U5's first attempt, withdrawn): the banner's surface — the wizard ready page — is a screen users see once, and a status that lives only there forces the failure into a first-run narrative the owner explicitly did not want. 设置 › 通用 is where the switch that governs this mode lives, so it is where the mode's truth belongs; the row also states the live stack's mode (spawn-time snapshot), which a boot-time banner structurally cannot.

## Evidence

The settings status row, every state it can honestly state, rendered by the real `GeneralSettings` component tree with the app's real `settings.css` loaded and the real `text.ts` dictionaries of head `63bebbc`, with a faked `sdShell` bridge answering the two IPC queries the row reads (round-14 styled set — the round-13 frames were plain DOM dumps proving copy only). The frames below the tables are refreshed at head `dc0b95a` (round-15): they show both UI increments from the author's real-machine feedback — the switch hint split into a lead sentence plus a「了解完整影响」`<details>` expander, and the status dot moved beside its sentence (row's right edge, vertically centred) instead of wrapping under the label:

**EN — probe passed, stack spawned sandboxed (default install) — green:**

![EN: green row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qingkwl/sciencediscovery/pr-1336-evidence/shots/14-en-ok.png)

**EN — opt-in at spawn, switch ON — opted-out, names the switch:**

![EN: opted-out row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qingkwl/sciencediscovery/pr-1336-evidence/shots/14-en-optedout.png)

**EN — stack spawned direct, switch since OFF — the restart applies it (F22/F24):**

![EN: switch-off row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qingkwl/sciencediscovery/pr-1336-evidence/shots/14-en-switchoff.png)

**EN — probe failed this session — amber, cause composed from `detail.failCode`, raw reason + diagnostics on the dot tooltip:**

![EN: failed row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qingkwl/sciencediscovery/pr-1336-evidence/shots/14-en-failed.png)

**EN — the adopted-stack window (F26): session attached to an already-running backend, mode inferred not verified — the row hedges:**

![EN: attached row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qingkwl/sciencediscovery/pr-1336-evidence/shots/14-en-attached.png)

**ZH — the switch-off window:**

![ZH: switch-off row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qingkwl/sciencediscovery/pr-1336-evidence/shots/14-zh-switchoff.png)

**ZH — attached (F26):**

![ZH: attached row](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qingkwl/sciencediscovery/pr-1336-evidence/shots/14-zh-attached.png)

Round-14 comment with the same frames: https://github.com/openJiuwen-ai/sciencediscovery/pull/1336#issuecomment-7119401764

- `pnpm --dir application test`: **362/362** (the gate's test cases retired with the gate; the probe's interpret/probe cases intact, reason copy reworded to match the no-gate reality).
- `pnpm --dir application typecheck` + desktop `tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- desktop pins (run on CI's linux host via the `os:linux` tag; also verified locally by lifting the tag): the wizard self-check list without the Seatbelt row, the absence of the five retired banner keys in both locales, the status row's six states (green / failed+cause / opted-out / both mid-session-toggle windows / no-row), the hint's full blast radius including the R cost, in both languages.
- api package: 302 cases, 0 fail (85 pass + 217 platform-tagged skips, same as the U1 baseline).
- Visual evidence (real frames, in the review thread below): the settings sandbox group — green row on a healthy install, the failed row with cause + diagnostics tooltip on a probe-failure session, the opted-out row on an opted-in install.

**Round-15 refresh at head `dc0b95a` — the two real-machine UI feedback increments:**

| zh ok — dot beside the sentence, lead-sentence hint with the「了解完整影响」expander | zh opted-out (switch ON) |
| --- | --- |
| ![15-zh-ok](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qingkwl/sciencediscovery/pr-1336-evidence/shots/15-zh-ok.png) | ![15-zh-optedout](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qingkwl/sciencediscovery/pr-1336-evidence/shots/15-zh-optedout.png) |

Failed (amber + cause) and attached (neutral blue) states carry the same right-edge dot: [15-zh-failed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qingkwl/sciencediscovery/pr-1336-evidence/shots/15-zh-failed.png) · [15-zh-attached](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qingkwl/sciencediscovery/pr-1336-evidence/shots/15-zh-attached.png) · [15-en-ok](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qingkwl/sciencediscovery/pr-1336-evidence/shots/15-en-ok.png).

## Non-goals

- No Intel/x64 anything; the flag is darwin-only and inert elsewhere (win32 hard-sets its own env; a plain browser has no bridge).
- No automatic unsandboxed **evolution** run: a probe failure degrades the session automatically (the Agent's Shell/Python and the stack itself then run unsandboxed — stated on the settings status row), but every evolution candidate run still requires the per-run confirmation in pre-flight. The automatic part is the session's own mode, never a candidate launch.
- No second Agent stack; no public API changes (the bridge additions are shell-internal).

A report's `[evidenceN]` chip opened 科学记忆 scoped to the report's Session, and the persisted chip references carried no owning Session. Citing a node created in an earlier Session of the same project therefore always showed "This memory was not found", implying the record was deleted.

## Changes
- Card-side fallback: read the citation's scope first; when nothing matches and the citation names no Session, read once unscoped and use the hit's `sessionId` for provenance. Budget refusals and an unreachable or disabled service stay "unavailable", never "missing".
- The unscoped read is limited to `GLOBALLY_UNIQUE_ID_LABELS` (`Artifact`, `Evidence`, `SourceFile`), whose node id is the record's own key. `DbRecord` is excluded on purpose: its id is the bare `identifier` and the graph keys those nodes by `(session_id, source, identifier)`, so a citation that names no Session returns `unlocated` instead of accepting a same-id record from another Session. The stale "Node ids are globally unique" comment now states this actual semantics.
- A page the sidecar cut short is not proof that nothing exists. `resolveCitation` carries `truncated` out of the scoped and the unscoped read alike and returns the new `unlocated` outcome instead of `missing`; `missing` is now reachable only from a page the sidecar did not cap.
- `memory.notFoundBody` (en/zh) now only says no record matches the citation; an outage keeps its own message, and `unlocated` has its own copy (`memory.unlocatedTitle` / `unlocatedBody`, en/zh) so it never renders the not-found sentence.
- New citations carry the owning Session: the sidecar's `cited_targets`/`chip_map` gain `session_id`, `toChipMap()` copies it, and the report reference persists it. Artifact chips keep none because the artifact dialog resolves them through the project.

## Validation
All numbers below were produced in the task checkout at head `c5ac07e1141e911971859730c8fe9973eb426968` (tree `aa11afc5302aec0f80fd67c2391f9f66524f81f3`), after `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`; each names the local log it comes from. The previous description's 1424/1424 figure belonged to the old head `76bf461c` and is not reused here.

- `pnpm build` — exit 0, 41 workspace projects (log: `.tmp/build.log`).

1345.body:
The session-level Idea Tree settings card stored parameters but started nothing, and the research card could go missing. Both are fixed, and the card now works the way the rest of the composer does: it puts a command token in the box instead of acting on it.

## 1. The card offers 确认 / 取消 / 覆盖全局设置, and says what they mean

`apps/desktop/src/views/idea/IdeaTreeOverrideDialog.tsx` drew four actions: 取消, 只用于本次会话, 跟随全局设置, 覆盖全局设置. 跟随全局设置 is gone; the card now draws exactly 确认, 取消 and 覆盖全局设置, and the hint states the contract: confirming applies these values to this conversation, puts the Idea Tree command in the composer, and leaves the global defaults alone; only 覆盖全局设置 writes the defaults.

The undo the removed button provided is visible instead of implicit: every row shows the deployment value it inherits (`全局：5`) and marks the ones this conversation has moved away from (`已覆盖`), so putting a field back to that value and confirming releases the pin — `saveSession`'s empty-diff path writes `{}`, which the Session normalizer reads as no override.

## 2. Confirming seeds the command; the reader sends it

Confirming used to close the card and send the message itself. That made it answer for things it cannot know — a turn already running drops the send without a word, and there was no objective yet — and it made the card the only place the research could start.

It now places `/idea-tree-team` in the composer as the existing blue command token, with the task the reader had already written under it. They complete the task and press send; that send starts the research, and the parameters are read at creation (`services/api/src/idea-tree/research.ts` calls `resolveIdeaTreeSettings(sessionId)`).

- A typed `/idea-tree` keeps its own command in the token, so the token never claims a different command than the one typed.
- A draft that is only a command contributes no task (`ideaTaskOf`), so `/idea-tree-team` followed by 会话设置 can no longer send `/idea-tree-team /idea-tree-team …`.
- A sent token is the confirmed pass: `sendMessage` composes the token and the task and never defers back into the card.
- With nothing written the token cannot be sent at all: the composer's send button and Enter both require a task, so the reader writes the question before anything leaves the box. The box asks for one in the token's own words.

## 3. Confirming is refused when it could not write

From the settings row the confirm is also the write, so it is offered only with a conversation open and a draft that was actually read: no Session, or a failed settings read, leaves 确认 disabled rather than placing a token that would run on the deployment values while the hint promises "these values". A command the reader typed still comes back to them as a token even when the read failed — that path writes nothing by design.

## 4. The research card no longer goes missing

`idea_research.created` sat in the run-stream reducer's deferred list, so the desktop ignored it. The list was only re-read while the command's five-minute waiting window was open, and a real model spends that long on preparation before it calls `create_idea_research` — after which nothing re-read the list and the card at the transcript's foot never appeared. The event is now counted (`run-stream/model.ts`, `reducer.ts`) and the app re-reads the list when it arrives, the same way `evolve_run.created` already did.

## 5. Documentation matches the card again

Both `docs/{zh,en}/developer-docs/desktop-frontend.md` described 只用于本次会话 and 跟随全局设置 → `null`. They now describe the three actions, the inherited-value rows, the release-by-reverting path, and the token the confirm seeds.

## Summary

Routes only **merge queue (`merge_group`)** runs of **`UT`** and the three heavy **L2 mocked E2E shards (`standard-config`, `standard-journeys`, `research`)** to self-hosted Docker runners (`[self-hosted, Linux, X64, sciencediscovery]`), gated behind the repository variable `CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE == 'true'` (default off).

Closes #1360

## Motivation

In merge-queue runs, `UT` and the three heavy L2 mocked E2E shards (`standard-config`, `standard-journeys`, `research`) dominate wall-clock time on GitHub-hosted runners and must complete before `L3 real E2E` starts. Moving just these four trusted merge-queue jobs onto dedicated Dockerized self-hosted runners with container-local caches speeds up queue throughput without exposing self-hosted runners to untrusted `pull_request` (or fork) runs or adding job duplication.

## Changes

- **`.ci/tier-policy.mjs`**:
  - Export `SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER = ['self-hosted', 'Linux', 'X64', 'sciencediscovery']`.
  - Compute `self_hosted_merge_queue = event === 'merge_group' && selfHostedMergeQueue === true` and `ut_runner` (`SELF_HOSTED_RUNNER` when enabled, otherwise `'ubuntu-latest'`). Non-`merge_group` events (`pull_request`, `workflow_dispatch`, `workflow_call`, `schedule`, `push`) always fail closed to `'ubuntu-latest'`.
- **`.ci/mocked-matrix.mjs`**:
  - Export `HEAVY_MOCKED_SHARDS` (`standard-config`, `standard-journeys`, `research`) and `buildMockedMatrix()`.
  - Include `runner` and `self_hosted` per shard so only the three heavy shards target self-hosted runners when `CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE=true`, while `governed` and `literature` stay on `ubuntu-latest`.
- **`.ci/use-local-swarm-cache.sh`**:
  - Manage a `flock`-serialized, content-hashed read-only JiuwenSwarm installation under `${SD_CI_CACHE_DIR:-/ci-cache}/jiuwenswarm/<key>/src`.
  - Strip `.git` after cold setup so `scripts/jiuwenswarm.sh setup` takes its pre-installed read-only fast path across concurrent runner containers while every job retains its own isolated `JIUWENSWARM_HOME` under `CI_RUNTIME_DIR`.
  - Export only `JIUWENSWARM_SRC` to `$GITHUB_ENV` (leaving `SCIENCE_AGENT_JIUWENSWARM_OVERRIDES` to callers that explicitly drive JiuwenSwarm).
- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`**:
  - Wire `vars.CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE` through `policy` -> `e2e-plan` / `ut` / `e2e`.
  - Raise mocked `e2e` `max-parallel` from `4` to `5` (allowing the 3 heavy self-hosted shards and 2 light hosted shards to run concurrently).
  - Skip cross-region `actions/cache` round trips (pnpm, uv, Playwright Chromium, JiuwenSwarm) only when a job is routed to a self-hosted runner, replacing JiuwenSwarm cache restore with `.ci/use-local-swarm-cache.sh`.
  - Make `Provision the bubblewrap sandbox` idempotent in `ut` and `e2e` by probing `bwrap --unshare-user --ro-bind / / --dev /dev true` before invoking `sudo apt-get` / `sudo sysctl`, so non-root pre-provisioned containers pass without requiring `sudo`.
- **`test/support/tagged/shared.mjs`**:
  - Export `sharedCacheEnv()` and honor pre-set `UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR`, `npm_config_cache`, and `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` (matching existing `UV_CACHE_DIR` handling) while preserving exact workspace-local fallbacks when unset.
- **`.ci/README.md`, `.ci/mocked-shards.test.mjs`, `.ci/self-hosted-merge-queue.test.mjs`**:
  - Document the optional `CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE` toggle and `max-parallel: 5`.
  - Add unit, CLI, workflow contract, and hermetic shell tests for routing, cache toggling, `sharedCacheEnv()`, and `.ci/use-local-swarm-cache.sh`.

## Safety & Rollout

- **Default off**: Merging this PR causes zero runner change while `vars.CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE` is unset; all PR and merge-queue jobs continue running on `ubuntu-latest`.
- **Event boundary**: `pull_request` (including forks), `workflow_dispatch`, `schedule`, `push`, light mocked shards (`governed`, `literature`), `ST`, desktop jobs, packaging, and real E2E jobs never route to self-hosted runners even when `CI_SELF_HOSTED_MERGE_QUEUE=true`.

1364.author: yuanzhou75
1364.body:
The nightly L4 case `test/journey-idea-tree-real.spec.ts` fails intermittently, and it failed for two different reasons that looked identical from the assertion.

## What the failures were

Run against `77b3a938` alone, on the same machine, three times:

| attempt | result | where it broke |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | fail | `Idea Tree 研究控制` not visible in 180s |
| 2 | fail | `Idea Tree 研究控制` not visible in 180s |
| 3 | fail | `researchById()` null, terminal wait timed out |

A separate control run on pure `main` failed once in two for the second reason, so neither failure belongs to any one PR: the case is flaky against this environment.

## Why the card could be missing

`apps/web/src/IdeaResearchCard.tsx` read the list once on mount, then refreshed only when `idea_research.created` arrived on the run stream, or over SSE while a research was already active. The created event is not replayed, so a client that was not listening at that instant — a reload, a reconnect, a stream that attached late — never re-read the list. The research existed, the Session had it, and the card was simply never drawn.

That is a product bug, not only a test problem: the same thing happens to a user who reloads at the wrong moment.

## The fix

- **The card re-reads an empty list** every 5s and stops as soon as an item appears, or after 5 minutes, so an idle conversation makes no requests. Two mounted tests pin it: the card appears with no event at all, and the timer stops once its window is spent.
- **The journey asserts the fact before the interface.** It now polls the API for exactly one new research (180s, as before), captures its id, and only then waits 60s for the card. "Nothing was created" and "the card did not draw it" can no longer produce the same failure.
- **A research that never settles says what it was doing**: the terminal poll reports the last status, phase, round and `reason` instead of a bare timeout.

The second failure mode — a research that stays `running` past 720s — is not addressed here beyond that reporting: it is agent/engine behaviour, and the next run will say whether it recurs and where it stalls.

## Tests

- `apps/web` suite: **1393 pass / 0 fail** (includes the two new mounted cases), `tsc -p apps/web/tsconfig.json --noEmit` clean.
- `test/check-e2e-meta.mjs`: 127 spec files, 0 errors.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.tests.json --noEmit` (root) clean.
- Real L4 runs are being executed against this head by the team's E2E runner; this PR stays a draft until the case passes repeatedly, and the run list will be added here.

Draft on purpose: a flakiness fix is only worth merging once the case is green several times in a row on a real stack with a live model.


## Update: the `blocked` run, not only the missing card

A live capture from the stack (`state.jsonl`, every 3s while the case ran) showed what the intermittent reds actually are: the run went `running` → **`blocked`** after 40s, `research_items` stayed empty for the whole case, and the timeout then cancelled the run. Nothing was created, so nothing could be drawn.

That is a second, independent cause, and it is in the journey: `createProjectAndSession` was called without `approvalMode`, while every other real journey on this stack passes `approvalMode: "always_allow"` — a headless run cannot press an approval card, and the agent's preparation can raise one. The journey now asks for the same mode, states it in E2E-META, and keeps the two earlier changes: the card re-reads an empty list (a real UI bug for a reloaded client), and the fact is asserted before the interface.

Re-running the case repeatedly on this head is the next step; the run list will be added here.

## What changed
- `设置 › 运行环境` now passes `{ client, key: "runner-catalog" }` to `useLoaded`, reusing the existing per-client `settings-cache`: a revisit paints the last catalog while the refresh runs behind it.
- `LoadGate` accepts an optional `skeleton`, used only on a cache miss. Pages without one keep the current loading line, and the error/retry plus "stale value under a visible failure" behaviour is unchanged.
- First paint is now layout-shaped: three metric cards and four table rows for `模型用量`, two Runner card rows for `运行环境`. Both regions use `role="status"`, `aria-busy` and a localized label, hide the blocks from assistive tech, and stop the shimmer under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
- Prefetch is deliberately omitted: without single-flight dedupe plus a freshness check it would only repeat the same two heavy reads.

## Verification
- Desktop unit suite: 1504 passed / 0 failed (137 suites), including new first-paint skeleton, cached-Runner paint and cross-client isolation cases.
- Baseline contrast on `e61b1d29` with the same test files: 55 passed / 3 failed — the new skeleton assertions fail there, so the tests distinguish the fix from the defect.
- New mocked E2E journeys hold `/api/runners` and `/api/usage/analytics`: skeleton visible on the first visit, remembered card/summary after switching away and back. 2/2 pass here; both fail on baseline at the skeleton assertion. Full `settings-interactions.spec.ts`: 38/38.
- `pnpm typecheck` clean, desktop build clean, and the other `LoadGate` panes (技能/网络/代理/配额) keep their unchanged loading line: 67/67.

## Remaining risk
Endpoint cost is unchanged: a first click still waits on live Runner probes or server-side usage aggregation, so ~1 s / ~1.5 s remains when no answer is cached. The skeleton and the loaded content are close but not pixel-identical, so a small layout shift remains on landing.
